newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico to unveil plans to finance development.
newsitem.headline: Mexico to unveil plans to finance development.

text.p: Mexico's President Ernesto Zedillo will unveil Tuesday a new National Program to Finance Development 1997-2000, with an underlying aim to create jobs, bring inflation down to single digits and boost the economy.

National media said Tuesday that the backbone of the three year plan will be to create one million jobs per year, bring annual inflation down below 10 percent and fuel the economy so that the gross domestic product (GDP) grows by at least five percent to the end of the millenium.
Pro-government TV network Televisa said Finance Minister Guillermo Ortiz and Labor Minister Javier Bonilla outlined those goals to union leaders late Monday. Televisa cited no direct sources.
Scant concrete details of the financing plan have been officially divulged by the government. Zedillo is scheduled to announce the plan at 0900 local (1400 GMT).

Daily Reforma said four key elements are to promote the recovery of purchasing power, boost domestic savings and direct private investment, give support and financing to medium- and small-sized businesses and combat poverty.
Radio network Radio Red concurred that the main thrust of the plan would be to boost growth and that there would be an announcement of new financing. It gave no details.
Radio Red said opposition parties were calling Zedillo's move an "electioneering plan." Zedillo's Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI) faces mid-term elections on July 6.

Control of Congress and part of the Senate are at stake. Mexico City residents will vote for the capital's mayor for the first time ever and a handful of state governors are also to be elected. Mexico City's mayor has previously been handpicked by the president.
